newsitem.title: USA: Illinois poll shows Clinton lead widening.
newsitem.headline: Illinois poll shows Clinton lead widening.

text.p: President Clinton widened his lead over Republican nominee Bob Dole among likely Illinois voters in the presidential election, according to a Chicago Tribune poll released Wednesday.

In the Oct. 25-27 poll of 900 registered voters who expect to vote in the Nov. 5 election, Clinton held a 55-28 margin over Dole, up from the presidential incumbent's 22-point lead in a survey taken three weeks earlier, the Tribune said.
Ross Perot's support rose to 8 percent from 6 percent from the last poll, with 9 percent still undecided against 12 percent previously. The poll's margin of error was 3 percent.

In the race to fill retiring Democrat Sen. Paul Simon's seat, the poll showed Democratic Congressman Richard Durbin extending his lead over millionaire Republican lawyer Al Salvi to 51-31, up from 42-35 in the earlier survey.
Eighteen percent of likely voters questioned on the Senate race remained undecided, down from 23 percent.
